description: The relationship rules a service_design_record.v1 is checked against (00_UniversalStandards/16_Service_Design_Record.md §6). A record names this rule set in rules_version; a consumer refuses a record naming a rule set it does not implement. Changing what a rule checks is a new rule set version, never an edit.

rules.title: Every component names the record's service.
SLI ids are unique and SLO ids are unique.
Every SLO names an SLI in the record.
The record has an SLO on an availability SLI and an SLO on a latency SLI.
An SLO target is strictly higher than its external commitment.
One outage lasting the RTO fits inside every SLO's error budget.
rules.limits: A floor only: it shows a single recovery cannot exhaust the budget, not that the target is achievable. DR-020 checks the target against the declared failure scenarios.

rules.title: Every store, and every cache's cached class, names a class in the table.
Every store meets its class's minimum copies, placement and replication.
A store whose class requires backup declares its backup.

Every backed-up store's worst-case recovery point is no longer than the RPO: the backup interval plus the time until a backup is restorable, and the replication lag of any asynchronous replica a failover could promote.
rules.limits: Checks the declared design only. Whether backups complete on time and restores work is shown by backup monitoring and restore tests, not by this rule.

rules.title: A region-scoped failover places every backed-up store in more than one region.
A store holding value data uses a strongly consistent class.
A cache uses a mode its cached class allows and a TTL within that class's staleness bound.
In-flight load at peak covers Little's Law: peak rate x P99 latency, rounded up.
Declared concurrency holds the in-flight load at peak.
Mean arrival rate does not exceed peak.
Total monthly cost is at least the sum of its parts.
Class ids in the table are unique.
No failure scenario's downtime is longer than the RTO.
Expected downtime from the declared failure scenarios fits every availability SLO's error budget.
rules.limits: Only as good as the declared scenarios, their yearly rates and downtimes; incident history should be used to correct them.
